blocks.intro: About 4 in 10 Evanston homes were built before 1940, and the city says most of its sewers are 80 to over 100 years old.

items.body: Short sections joined every two or three feet. Each joint is a doorway for roots.
Evanston's parkway canopy is beautiful and thirsty. Roots follow the moisture straight into old pipe.
The pipe that leaves the house is often cast iron, and it rusts through along the bottom.
The City of Evanston maintains the main. The pipe from your house to it is your responsibility.

blocks.h2: How We Repair a Sewer Line
blocks.intro: Once we know what's wrong, there's usually more than one way to fix it. Which method makes sense depends on the pipe's condition, location, and how it failed.
head: Method
What It Involves
Typical Disruption
rows: A resin-coated liner is pulled through the existing pipe and cured in place, creating a new pipe inside the old one.
Minimal digging, usually just small access points
A new pipe is pulled through the old one while a bursting head fractures the old pipe outward to make room.
Minimal digging, works even when the old pipe is badly damaged
The damaged section is dug up and replaced directly.
More digging, but sometimes the only option depending on damage location and access
blocks.note: Evanston laterals often cross the parkway under a city tree. Trenchless methods can protect the tree and the sidewalk.

blocks.h2: Sewer Repair Questions From Evanston Homeowners

items.q: Who is responsible for the sewer line in Evanston?
items.answer: The City of Evanston says sewer laterals are the property owner's responsibility. The city maintains the main in the street.

items.q: Do I have to replace the whole line?
items.preview: Not if only part is damaged.
items.answer: No. Many old laterals need one section repaired. A [camera inspection](/evanston/video-camera-sewer-inspections) shows how much is bad.

items.q: Can you repair the line without cutting the parkway tree?
items.answer: Often. [Trenchless repair](/evanston/trenchless-sewer-repair) works through small openings and leaves root zones mostly undisturbed.

items.q: Didn't the city's sewer project fix backups?
items.preview: It added capacity to the city system, not to your lateral.
items.answer: The city built relief sewers between 1991 and 2008. That work helps the public system, but a broken or root-filled lateral can still back up your basement.
Yes. Sewer work in Evanston usually needs a permit, and we handle it for the work we do.

items.q: Should I fix the lateral before I finish my basement?
items.preview: Yes, if the camera shows damage.
items.answer: Yes. Fixing it first means you won't have to cut through a new floor later.

items.q: How much does sewer repair cost in Evanston?
items.preview: It depends on the damage and method. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on what the camera finds, the depth, the method and what's above the line. You'll approve a flat-rate price before any work.
